title: The Base Model Is Dead — Varun Singh, Arcee AI

primary.label: Model Foundations & Behavior
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 84%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk discusses foundational LLM training methodology applicable across all application domains, with no specific vertical focus.

summary: Varun Singh, Pre-training Lead at Arcee AI, argues that the classical notion of a base model as a mirror of the internet is outdated. Historically, models like GPT-3 trained predominantly on web text (~85% of the training mix), with post-training adapting to chat and RL as a minor enhancement ("a cherry on top"). The release of OpenAI's o1 (2024) and DeepSeek R1 (January 2025) shifted RL from optional to central, demanding that base models carry priors RL can build on. Singh examines two contrasting open recipes: MAI Thinking 1 (Microsoft AI) avoids synthetic data entirely yet still reduces web text to ~15% (verified at 14.9% via official technical report), emphasizing code (54.6%) and STEM; Nemotron 3 Ultra pulls SFT-style Q&A data into pre-training to teach downstream task shapes early. Code data, absent in GPT-3, now dominates modern pre-training. Synthetic data methods include Trinity Lodge's rephrasing-based upsampling and Kimi K2's broad synthetic data application across pre-training. MOE load balancing is destabilized when post-training data distribution differs sharply from pre-training, motivating earlier introduction of post-training-flavored data. A mid-training stage has emerged for longer-context agentic traces. Singh reframes LM training as two paradigms—supervised next-token prediction and RL—with RL's compute share growing (Xiaomi MiMo Labs uses roughly equal allocation; Composer 2.5 spent heavily on RL). He concludes that base models have moved from general world knowledge priors to reasoning and agentic behavior priors, and should be designed as priors for whatever paradigm emerges next.
whyItMatters: These concepts form a coherent narrative about the evolution of base model design. The foundational paradigm—next-token prediction on web text for world knowledge (GPT-3 era)—is being replaced because RL became a central capability driver after o1 and DeepSeek R1. This shift demands that base models carry reasoning and agentic behavior priors rather than just world knowledge, which in turn drives concrete engineering changes: pre-training data mixtures shift from 85% web text to 15% with code dominance, synthetic data rephrasing pipelines enable controlled upsampling, SFT-style data is pulled into pre-training to teach task shapes early, and MOE load balancing must be managed across the shifting pre-training-to-post-training boundary. The two-paradigm framing (supervised vs RL) with growing RL compute share provides the theoretical lens, while atomic skill composition explains the mechanism by which pre-training data choices enable downstream RL exploration. Together, these concepts describe a complete rethinking of what base models are, how they are built, and what they must provide for the next generation of LLM training.
temporalContext: The video was published on July 31, 2026, and research was conducted as of August 23, 2026. The talk references developments from 2020 (GPT-3) through early 2025 (DeepSeek R1 in January 2025), with case studies including MAI Thinking 1 (released June 2026), Kimi K2 (July 2025), and Composer 2.5 (May 2026). The discussion reflects the state of LLM pre-training methodology as of mid-2026, capturing a rapid evolution in the field where open recipe publications have accelerated, enabling analysis of training data composition trends across model generations.
takeaways: The base model is no longer a mirror of the internet; web text dropped from ~85% (GPT-3) to ~15% (MAI Thinking 1) of training data.
RL shifted from a minor post-training flavor adjustment to a central capability driver after o1 and DeepSeek R1, changing what the base model must provide.
Two contrasting approaches exist: MAI Thinking 1 uses no synthetic data but still radically reduces web text; Nemotron 3 Ultra pulls SFT-style data into pre-training.
Code data, absent in GPT-3, now dominates modern pre-training recipes.
Synthetic data via rephrasing (Trinity Lodge) and broad application (Kimi K2) lets teams upsample, clean, and shape tokens toward instruct/agentic tasks from pre-training onward.
MOE load balancing is destabilized when post-training data distribution differs sharply from pre-training; pulling post-training-flavored data earlier helps establish stable representations.
RL compute is growing relative to supervised learning—Xiaomi Mimo Labs uses roughly equal allocation; Composer 2.5 spent more on RL than supervised learning.
Base models have moved from general world knowledge priors to reasoning and agentic behavior priors; if a new paradigm emerges, the base model should be built as a prior for that paradigm.
Some labs introduce novel data shapes like reasoning traces and test-time compute schemes during SFT or even pre-training to prepare models for RL exploration.

concepts.name: Base model role evolution
concepts.explanation: The conceptual shift in what a base model is for: from a general world-knowledge mirror trained on web text to a prior-building system designed to carry reasoning and agentic behavior capabilities that RL can build upon.
concepts.importance: The central thesis of the talk; redefines the foundational object of LLM training and has direct implications for how all subsequent training stages are designed.

concepts.name: RL as central capability driver
concepts.explanation: The transition from RL being a minor post-training flavor adjustment ('cherry on top') to a major driver of model capability, triggered by o1 and DeepSeek R1, fundamentally changing what the base model must provide.
concepts.importance: The pivotal inflection point in the talk's narrative; explains why base model design had to change and what the new requirements are.

concepts.name: Two-paradigm framing of LM training
concepts.explanation: Reframing language model training as two paradigms—supervised next-token prediction and reinforcement learning—with RL's compute share growing, raising the question of whether RL might eventually dominate as it did for AlphaGo.
concepts.importance: Provides the intellectual framework for the entire talk, connecting current trends to a potential future trajectory and motivating the shift in base model design.

concepts.name: Atomic skill composition for RL
concepts.explanation: The idea that the base model needs prior exposure to atomic skills that RL can compose during exploration, meaning pre-training data must include building blocks for the capabilities RL will develop.
concepts.importance: Bridges pre-training and RL conceptually, explaining why code, STEM, and reasoning traces matter in pre-training even when RL is the primary capability driver.

concepts.name: Reasoning and agentic behavior priors
concepts.explanation: The new class of priors that base models must carry, replacing general world knowledge priors: specifically, representations that support reasoning chains and agentic tool-use behaviors that RL can refine.
concepts.importance: Defines the target outcome of modern base model design and explains the specific data choices (code dominance, reasoning traces, SFT-style data in pre-training).

concepts.name: Test-time compute warming in pre-training
concepts.explanation: The practice of introducing data shapes and training schemes during SFT or even pre-training that prepare models for test-time compute strategies, as referenced in the Ziya paper context.
concepts.importance: Represents a forward-looking technique for aligning base models with inference-time reasoning, though the specific Ziya reference could not be fully verified against external sources.

concepts.name: Model collapse risk from synthetic data
concepts.explanation: The danger that blindly injecting synthetic data into training can cause model collapse and performance degradation, requiring careful curation and quality control of synthetic data pipelines.
concepts.importance: A key limitation and cautionary consideration that constrains how aggressively synthetic data can be used in pre-training, balancing the benefits of upsampling against quality risks.

concepts.name: Next-token prediction as world knowledge acquisition
concepts.explanation: The classical mechanism by which pre-training on large-scale web text accumulates world knowledge and builds internal representations through the supervised next-token prediction objective.
concepts.importance: The foundational paradigm that Singh argues is no longer sufficient, serving as the baseline against which the new reasoning/agentic prior paradigm is contrasted.

concepts.name: Pre-training data mixture engineering
concepts.explanation: The deliberate design and proportioning of training data domains (code, STEM, web text, books, synthetic) in pre-training, moving from ad-hoc web-scraping to principled domain allocation strategies optimized for downstream RL readiness.
concepts.importance: Central to the talk's thesis; the shift from 85% web text (GPT-3) to 15% (MAI Thinking 1) represents a fundamental engineering rethinking of what tokens go into a base model and why.

concepts.name: Synthetic data rephrasing pipeline
concepts.explanation: A data engineering technique where seed data items are rephrased at web scale to produce multiple surface forms of the same information, enabling the model to see identical content expressed differently, improving robustness and representation quality.
concepts.importance: Demonstrated by Trinity Lodge (Arcee AI) as a concrete engineering method for upsampling seed data without naive duplication, directly shaping pre-training data quality.

concepts.name: SFT data integration into pre-training
concepts.explanation: The practice of pulling supervised fine-tuning style question-answer data directly into the pre-training stage, so the model learns the shape of downstream tasks from the beginning rather than only during post-training.
concepts.importance: Represents a structural rethinking of the pre-training/post-training boundary, exemplified by Nemotron 3 Ultra, and directly addresses the problem of distribution mismatch between stages.

concepts.name: MOE load balancing engineering
concepts.explanation: Managing the distribution of tokens across expert modules in Mixture-of-Experts architectures during training, including adjusting load-balancing coefficients when data distribution shifts between pre-training and post-training stages.
concepts.importance: A concrete engineering challenge discussed as destabilizing when post-training data differs sharply from pre-training; MAI Thinking 1 had to crank up load-balancing coefficients during SFT, which Singh argues is suboptimal so late in training.

concepts.name: Mid-training stage design
concepts.explanation: An emerging training stage between pre-training and post-training, focused on longer-context agentic traces, using re-weighted pre-training corpus data to bridge the gap between base knowledge and downstream task requirements.
concepts.importance: Represents a new engineering stage in the training pipeline; Singh argues it could be absorbed into pre-training, reflecting ongoing debate about optimal stage boundaries.

concepts.name: Compute allocation engineering
concepts.explanation: The strategic distribution of compute budget between supervised pre-training and reinforcement learning post-training, with the trend showing RL's share growing relative to supervised learning.
concepts.importance: Quantified in the talk via Xiaomi MiMo Labs (roughly equal split) and Composer 2.5 (more RL than supervised), illustrating a shift in how training resources are allocated.

sections.title: The base model as a mirror of the web
sections.summary: Singh introduces the classical view: base models trained on large-scale web text reflect human internet knowledge. Pre-training accumulates world knowledge and builds representations through next-token prediction. Post-training shapes the model for chat interfaces, and RL is a minor flavor adjustment.

sections.title: Historical data mixes: GPT-3 to Llama 3
sections.summary: GPT-3's training mix was ~85% web text (Common Crawl, WebText-2, Wikipedia). Llama 3 still used 50% general knowledge web text. Post-training was mostly adapting to chat templates and Q&A format, with RL as a cherry on top rather than conferring new capabilities.

sections.title: After o1: RL becomes central
sections.summary: OpenAI's o1 (2024) and DeepSeek R1 (Jan 2025) pioneered reasoning models, making RL a major capability driver rather than a topping. Cloud Code and agentic use cases further expanded RL's role. The question becomes whether the standard base model is still the best prior for this new RL-heavy paradigm.

sections.title: Reading open data recipes: MAI Thinking 1 vs Nemotron
sections.summary: Two contrasting approaches: MAI Thinking 1 uses no synthetic data yet reduces web text to 15%, emphasizing code and STEM. Nemotron 3 Ultra pulls SFT-style Q&A data into pre-training to teach downstream task shapes early. Code, absent in GPT-3, now dominates pre-training recipes.

sections.title: Synthetic data methods and benefits
sections.summary: Trinity Lodge used synthetic rephrasing to upsample seed data. Kimi K2 applied synthetic data broadly across pre-training. Swallow Code/Math showed early benefits. Synthetic data provides more tokens, higher quality, and task-shaped representations from the start of pre-training.

sections.title: MOE load balancing and mid-training
sections.summary: MOE training faces load-balancing instability when post-training data distribution differs from pre-training. MAI Thinking 1 compensated by cranking load-balancing coefficients during SFT. Singh argues post-training data should be introduced earlier for stable representations. A mid-training stage has emerged for longer-context agentic traces but could be absorbed into pre-training.

sections.title: Two paradigms: supervised learning and RL
sections.summary: Singh reframes LM training as supervised next-token prediction and RL, with RL's compute share growing. Xiaomi Mimo Labs allocates roughly equal compute to pre- and post-training; Composer 2.5 used more RL than supervised learning. Research suggests the base model needs exposure to atomic skills for RL composition. The AlphaGo trajectory raises the question of whether RL might eventually dominate for language models.

sections.title: Conclusion: From world priors to reasoning and agentic priors
sections.summary: Singh discusses labs introducing novel data during supervised learning, such as reasoning traces whose shape differs from typical human output, and warming models to test-time compute schemes during SFT or even pre-training, referencing Zephyr's Ziya 1 paper. He concludes that base models have moved from general human knowledge and world priors to reasoning and agentic behavior priors. If a new interaction paradigm were to emerge, the base model should be conceived as building a prior for that paradigm rather than merely training on a massive script of web text.

organization.name: Arcee AI
organization.summary: Arcee AI is an American research lab founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, CA. The company builds open-weight foundation models with a full-stack ML research approach encompassing data, pre-training, post-training, serving, and evaluation. Their model families include Trinity and AFM. The company has approximately 32 employees and has raised $29.5M in total funding, including a strategic investment from Prosperity 2 (Microsoft's Venture Fund) with participation from Hitachi. Arcee AI's research philosophy emphasizes performance per parameter, open weights, and end-to-end pipeline ownership. Their Hugging Face organization (arcee-ai) has 50 public repositories and 624 followers.
organization.status: Active; developing open-weight models including the Trinity and AFM families; recently secured strategic funding round led by Microsoft's Prosperity 2 venture fund

sources.title: AI Model Catalog | Microsoft Foundry Models - MAI-Thinking-1

technologies.label: MAI-Thinking-1 Model Family
technologies.summary: MAI-Thinking-1 is Microsoft AI's reasoning model built from scratch as a 35B active / 1T total sparse MoE Transformer, trained on 30T pre-training tokens with a data mix of 54.6% code, 15.8% STEM, 5.4% math (sampled 5.28x), and only 14.9% web text. It uses no LM-generated synthetic data, yet still radically reduces web text from the GPT-3 era's ~85%. A mid-training stage of 3.55T tokens uses re-weighted pre-training corpus data only. The talk uses MAI-Thinking-1 as the primary case study for how base model data recipes have shifted toward code, STEM, and reasoning-shaped data, and as an example of MOE load-balancing challenges when post-training distribution diverges from pre-training.
technologies.role: Primary open recipe case study demonstrating the shift from web text dominance to code and STEM dominance in pre-training data, with verified data composition figures and MOE load-balancing challenges

technologies.label: Kimi K2 Model Family
technologies.summary: Kimi K2 is Moonshot AI's 1T parameter MoE model with 32B activated parameters, pre-trained on 15.5T tokens using the MuonClip optimizer for zero training instability. Unlike MAI-Thinking-1, Kimi K2 broadly incorporates synthetic data generation across its pre-training pipeline at larger scale. The talk uses Kimi K2 as a contrasting case study to MAI-Thinking-1, showing that even with synthetic data, the trend away from web text and toward code and agentic capabilities holds. Kimi K2's agentic intelligence focus also exemplifies the shift toward agentic behavior priors in base models.
technologies.role: Contrasting case study to MAI-Thinking-1, demonstrating broad synthetic data application in pre-training and agentic intelligence focus

technologies.label: Trinity Model Family
technologies.summary: Trinity is Arcee AI's open-weight model family (Large, Mini, and Nano variants) whose pre-training was led by the speaker Varun Singh. Referenced as 'Trinity Lodge' in the transcript, it pioneered web-scale synthetic rephrasing to upsample seed data items, enabling the model to encounter the same information in multiple surface forms without naive duplication. This technique represents a distinct approach to synthetic data in pre-training compared to Kimi K2's broad application, focusing on controlled quality augmentation rather than volume scaling. The speaker's direct experience with Trinity informs the talk's practical perspective on synthetic data methods.
technologies.role: Speaker's own model family demonstrating synthetic data rephrasing as a pre-training data upsampling technique, providing first-hand practitioner perspective

technologies.label: Composer 2.5
technologies.summary: Composer 2.5 is an agentic coding model developed by Cursor (Anysphere, Inc.) on Moonshot's Kimi K2.5 open-source checkpoint. It is trained with targeted reinforcement learning using textual feedback and 25x more synthetic tasks than its predecessor Composer 2. The talk cites Composer 2.5 as evidence that RL compute is growing relative to supervised learning, with the speaker claiming it used more RL compute than the model had ever seen in supervised learning. While the official Cursor blog confirms heavy RL training, it does not explicitly state that RL compute exceeded supervised learning compute, introducing some uncertainty into this specific quantitative claim.
technologies.role: Case study illustrating the growing RL compute share in model training, cited alongside Xiaomi MiMo as evidence that RL is becoming a central rather than supplementary training paradigm

Identify how open recipes (MAI Thinking 1, Nemotron 3 Ultra, Kimi K2) reflect the trend away from raw web text toward code, STEM, and synthetic data
Recognize why pulling post-training-flavored data into pre-training helps with MOE stability and task representation

Describe the emergence of a mid-training stage for longer-context agentic traces and its relationship to pre-training
Articulate why base models have shifted from world knowledge priors to reasoning and agentic behavior priors and should adapt to emerging paradigms
challengeSeeds: Design a pre-training data recipe for a reasoning-focused 10B parameter MoE model with a 20T token budget, specifying domain proportions and synthetic data strategy
Diagnose and fix MOE load-balancing collapse in a training log where expert utilization diverges sharply after SFT begins, proposing a mid-training or pre-training data intervention

Compare the data strategies of MAI Thinking 1 (no synthetic data, 15% web text) and Kimi K2 (broad synthetic data, 15.5T tokens) and argue which approach scales better under quality-constrained token budgets

Implement a synthetic data rephrasing pipeline that takes seed documents and generates multiple paraphrased versions, then measure whether a small model trained on the upsampled data shows improved task-shape learning versus a control
